activity.finding: Steps, workouts and active energy arrive from Apple Health or your wearable.
activity.headline: —
activity.method: Daily steps, exercise minutes and active energy: today, 7-day and 28-day means.
activity.title: Activity

body.finding: Blood oxygen, breathing rate and skin temperature come from a watch or ring worn overnight.
body.headline: —
body.method: Overnight SpO₂, breathing rate and skin temperature against your own 28-day baselines; the strain flag counts how many of resting HR, HRV, breathing rate and temperature moved the adverse way past one SD last night.
body.title: Body signals

fitness.finding: VO2 max and heart-rate recovery come from Apple Watch workouts outdoors; the app sends them with your walking data.
fitness.headline: —
fitness.method: VO2 max as Apple estimates it from outdoor walks and runs (90-day trend, first vs last month); one-minute heart-rate recovery after workouts; resting heart rate as the slow proxy. The band is a coarse population table by age and sex.
fitness.title: Cardio fitness

hrv.finding: HRV needs a device worn overnight (Apple Watch, Oura, WHOOP, Garmin).
hrv.headline: —
hrv.method: Nightly HRV, ln-transformed for the seven-day mean and the 28-day baseline; the smallest worthwhile change is half the baseline SD; balance is the 7-day mean over the 28-day mean; trend is the OLS slope over 14 days.
hrv.title: HRV

load.finding: Load needs active energy, workouts or steps from your device.
load.headline: —
load.method: Daily load from active energy (else exercise minutes, else steps). Acute and chronic are exponentially weighted averages with 7- and 28-day spans; ACWR is their ratio. Fitness and fatigue follow Banister (42- and 7-day constants), form is fitness minus fatigue. Monotony is the 7-day mean over its SD of the load above your everyday floor (the 28-day 20th percentile); strain is that weekly load times monotony (Foster).
load.title: Training load

overreach.finding: Needs a week of readiness, load and sleep to judge.
overreach.headline: —
overreach.method: Points for each sign present this week: seven-day readiness under 40 or 30, acute:chronic at 1.3 or 1.5, monotony over 2, form below −25 % of fitness, resting HR +2 or +4 bpm over baseline, seven-day HRV under its band, sleep debt over 2 or 4 h, soreness over 6/10. Capped at 100. Watch from 25, flag from 50.
overreach.title: Overreach watch

readiness.finding: Readiness needs today's HRV or resting heart rate and last night's sleep. Wear your watch overnight and sync in the morning.
readiness.headline: —
readiness.method: Weighted z-scores against your own 28-day baselines (ln-HRV 40 %, resting HR 25 %, sleep vs need 25 %, breathing rate and skin temperature 5 % each), mapped to 0–100 with a logistic curve. 50 is your normal; one SD off, taken together, is the edge of the green or red band.
readiness.title: Readiness

resting_hr.finding: Resting heart rate arrives from a watch or ring worn overnight.
resting_hr.headline: —
resting_hr.method: Nightly resting heart rate against your own 28-day baseline; the seven-day mean is compared to the baseline mean and SD.
resting_hr.title: Resting heart rate

rhythm.finding: Regularity needs bedtimes from your sleep tracker or hourly steps from your phone.
rhythm.headline: —
rhythm.method: Bedtime and wake regularity from the sleep panel; interdaily stability (van Someren) over hourly steps, 1.0 being a perfectly repeated day.
rhythm.title: Rhythm

sleep.finding: Sleep arrives from a watch or ring worn overnight, or from Health.
sleep.headline: —
sleep.method: Sleep need is your 28-night median (or your target) plus up to an hour after a heavy day. Debt is the last seven nights' shortfall against need, older nights discounted 15 % a night. Consistency is the circular SD of bedtime and wake time over 14 nights; efficiency is time asleep over time in bed.
sleep.title: Sleep

subjective.finding: Answer the daily check-in and your energy, soreness and mood sit here beside the wearable numbers.
subjective.headline: —
subjective.method: Your check-in answers over the last seven days: latest and average.
subjective.title: How you feel
